method: Grouped held-out permutation importance, 100 shuffles per group within each of the five test folds; exact existing fold-specific interaction regressions. Difference in fractional-label log loss, averaged over all battles and shuffles.

groups.Model identity: Jointly shuffle the model-identity contrast vector, equivalent to moving model A/B as a pair.
groups.Speed (TPS): Shuffle log2 TPS ratio and recompute speed × early using the unchanged early flag.
groups.Early vote: Shuffle the battle-level early-vote boolean and recompute speed × early using the unchanged speed ratio.

intervals: 95% developer-block bootstrap intervals on mean per-battle loss increase, 5000 draws. Conditional on fixed fitted models and permutation averages; no retraining.
interpretation: Larger means greater predictive reliance by this fitted model. Groups are correlated and interact: importances are not additive, not shares of variance, and not causal effects. Marginal shuffles can create identity/speed combinations unlike observed data.
validation: Each battle predicted without its own outcome in training; developers may occur in training and test. Early status is only known afterward.
